messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) pure water freezes at a temperature well below its normal 0 °C melting point.  
According to the water‑phase diagram, the solid–liquid equilibrium line at 10 kPa lies at roughly **–20 °C** (more precisely –19.9 °C for pure water).  

So, the freezing point of water at 10 kPa is about **–20 °C**.
